tip: Verbs whose infinitive ends in -a keep that -a in the command form: våga = dare.
Verbs with a consonant-final stem drop the infinitive -a in the command: försöka becomes försök = try.
The command form of vara (to be) is var, not är: var modig = be brave.
Slappna av = relax. The particle av is stressed and stays right after the verb.
Swedish has no separate word for the; an en-word adds -en: stol becomes stolen = the chair.
An en-word already ending in -a adds only -n for the: lampa becomes lampan = the lamp.
An ett-word adds -t for the: garage becomes garaget = the garage.
The plural the ending is -na: tallrikar (plates) becomes tallrikarna = the plates.
In a definite noun phrase, front det, give the adjective -a, and keep the noun's suffix: det svenska samhället = the Swedish society.
Bli plus a past participle forms a passive: har blivit stulen = has been stolen.
Adding -s to the supine makes a passive: förbättrats = had been improved.
In a main clause an adverb sits after the finite verb, before the main verb: har fullständigt missat = have completely missed.
Fronting the object for emphasis pushes the subject after the verb: Det här problemet måste vi lösa.
When a clause with medan comes first, the main clause begins with its verb: lagade hon mat.
After varför in a reported question there is no inversion: varför du är, never varför är du.
Swedish uses the present tense for future actions: ringer and kommer here mean will call and will arrive.
Om means whether in a reported yes/no question: frågar om hon vill = ask whether she wants to.
Som is the all-purpose relative word for who, which or that: restaurangen som ligger = the restaurant that is located.
When som is the object of its clause you may drop it: Filmen (som) vi såg = the film we saw.
In a subordinate clause inte comes before the verb: att han inte hade rätt, not att han hade inte.
Eftersom means because and opens a reason clause: eftersom det var sent = because it was late.
Berätta needs för before the listener: berättade för honom = told him.
Ha rätt, literally to have right, means to be right: hon har rätt = she is right.
Vänta takes på for what you wait for: vänta på mig = wait for me.
Hjälpa uses med for the task: hjälp din syster med läxorna = help your sister with the homework.
Få reda på is a fixed phrase meaning to find out: fick reda på = found out.
Se ut att means to seem or look like: ser ut att regna = looks like it will rain.
För att plus an infinitive expresses purpose, in order to: för att bli läkare = to become a doctor.
Klockan plus a number gives clock time: klockan åtta = at eight o'clock.
Lite means some or a little with uncountable nouns: lite mjölk = some milk, with no plural.
To feel well uses the verb må, not känna: han mår bra = he is doing well.
The suffix -bar works like English -able: hörbar = audible, from höra plus -bar.
Man is the generic subject for people in general: man säger = they say or one says.
Det finns is the set phrase for there is or there are: finns det andra fördelar = there are other advantages.
Add -t to an adjective to turn it into an adverb: hög becomes högt = aloud in läs högt.
